thread:
alyssa: Heads up — npm audit started failing on CI after the rollup plugin bump. Looks like a ReDoS in css-what (via css-select/cheerio). High severity flagged and CI is blocking on master. @jon can you take a look?

jon: On it. Which package exactly? css-what is transitive, right? I don't see it as a direct dep in console-ui.

alyssa: npm audit output (trimmed):
```
High        Regular Expression Denial of Service
Package     css-what
Patched in  >= 5.0.1
Dependency of stylelint > postcss-selector-parser > css-select > css-what
Path        console-ui > stylelint > postcss-selector-parser > css-select > css-what
More info   https://npmjs.com/advisories/1234567
```

ci-bot: Build failed: npm audit detected vulnerabilities. CI log: https://ci.redwood.internal/console-ui/12345 :warning:

jon: Got it. That chain makes sense — we recently bumped postcss-selector-parser in the stylelint upgrade PR (#4720). Could have pulled a css-select/cs-what combo that's flagged.

mike: Quick risk note: the vulnerability is ReDoS in a CSS parser. For our product that parses internal stylesheet files during build, attack surface is low (no user-supplied CSS parsed server-side). So customer-exploit risk is low, but we need to fix for dependency hygiene and to keep CI green.

alyssa: Agreed. Proposed plan: try a targeted bump to get css-what >=5.0.1 (via css-select bump) in a branch. If that works run full CI; otherwise pin with package overrides/resolutions to avoid broad lockfile churn. I'll open an internal triage ticket and mark severity high for now.

jon: Quick local check: `npm ls css-what` shows 4.1.0 (via stylelint chain) and 5.0.0 elsewhere. I'll attempt to bump css-select to 5.x in a sandbox to see compatibility surface. If css-select 5 requires stylelint major, we can apply an override for css-what only.

sam: FYI — because we use npm ci + package-lock v2, running `npm audit fix` can produce a lot of unrelated lockfile churn. We should avoid sweeping fixes on main. Use `overrides` in package.json or `npm-force-resolutions` in the short term to minimize churn.

jon: Trying overrides locally. Adding to package.json:
```
"overrides": {
  "css-what": "5.0.2"
}
```
Local build + test suite run looks green so far. No obvious runtime issues in the UI.

alyssa: If we go with overrides, capture the rationale in the PR and the security tracker (advisory-2026-01-csswhat internal ticket). Also include test matrix results and a note about why this is low-risk for runtime exploitation. We'll want to backport the fix to active release branches.

jon: I opened a minimal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/5012 — package.json override + package-lock update. CI run is queued.

mike: DRI: jon to author PR, alyssa to approve from security, sam to watch CI. Target: merge to main today and backport to release/2026-02 by EOD tomorrow if green.

alyssa: Suggested PR description blurb: "Mitigation: pin css-what to >=5.0.1 using package.json overrides to address npm advisory (Regular Expression DoS). No service-exposed parsing of user CSS; low exploitability. Backport planned to active release branches."

jon: CI passed on the PR, diff shows only the override and minimal lockfile changes. Merging now.

ci-bot: Merged and deployment to staging started. Logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/console-ui/12346 :rocket:

sam: Lockfile churn looks minimal, good job keeping changes scoped. I'll coordinate the backport to release/2026-02 after lunch.

alyssa: I'll update the internal advisory and mark it resolved once the release backport is cut. No evidence of in-the-wild exploit for our environment. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
